subject: Private offer: SKU packaging, overage protection & channel margin routing
messages:
From: Alice Wong <alice@borealishealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-17T09:12:00Z
Subject: Align on private offer packaging and partner crediting

Hi Sergio —

Thanks again for the demo last week. The team is excited to move to a private offer on GCP but we need clarity on three items before procurement will sign:

1) SKU granularity — our security team prefers a single metered SKU (tokens/hour) rather than multiple feature SKUs. Will that impact your ability to offer tiered discounts?
2) Overage protection — can Redwood provide a consumption buffer or overage credits if we spike beyond committed usage in Q1?
3) Channel margin routing — we need the reseller margin documented on the PO path (our reseller expects a 10–12% net). How is that reflected on the private offer and subsequent invoices?

Procurement asked that we have a one-page summary of final packaging and how the margin passes through to the reseller for their approval. Can you send that and a quick ETA?

Best,
Alice Wong
Head of Cloud Procurement
Borealis Health

P.S. CC'ing procurement inbox: procurement@borealishealth.com for timelines and PO contact.

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice@borealishealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-17T12:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Align on private offer packaging and partner crediting

Alice —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up front and then a proposed next step:

- SKU granularity: We can do a single metered SKU (tokens) for the private offer and still support tiered commit discounts. The private offer will map the commit bands to token rates; we'll include a table in the PO so procurement can see rate changes by tier.
- Overage protection: We offer two options: 1) automatic buffer (5–15% depending on commit level) applied as bill credit after month close, or 2) pre-purchased burst capacity that sits as an add-on SKU. For a health provider with spiky usage we usually recommend the buffer credit to avoid procurement complications.
- Channel margin routing: For marketplace private offers, the reseller margin is represented as a separate line on our billing paperwork and flagged in the private-offer metadata so it shows up on downstream invoices. We can confirm exact percent and whether that's net or gross routing.

I've attached a draft SKU matrix that maps a single token-based SKU to tiered rates and shows how a 10% reseller credit would be passed. Please see "Borealis-SKU-matrix-v3.xlsx" attached.

Next step: If you agree to the single-SKU + buffer-credit approach, Ben (cc) will propose the reseller routing and I can put together the one-page summary for procurement and a DocuSign private offer. Can we target COB Thursday for sign-off?

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Strategic Accounts — Cloud Marketplaces
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Borealis-SKU-matrix-v3.xlsx

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: alice_wong <alice@borealishealth.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-18T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Align on private offer packaging and partner crediting

Alice / Sergio —

Agree on single-token SKU as the simplest procurement path. A few specifics on channel margin and routing:

- Reseller margin: We can document a 11% reseller margin as a separate credit line item on the private offer metadata; this will flow through GCP's settlement and should be visible to Borealis' reseller.
- Invoice path: Redwood issues the gross invoice to Borealis; GCP marketplace processes the reseller passback to the partner. We'll include the reseller tax treatment note if you need it for audit.
- Overage handling: Recommend buffer credit at 10% for your initial commit size. If you'd prefer pre-purchased burst capacity instead, we can add a small add-on SKU at a discounted rate.

I've added the deal to HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/83421/deal/DEAL-2027-0843. Procurement, what's your typical PO cadence? If you can route a PO by next Tue we can lock pricing and start the DocuSign flow.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Marketplace Sales
Redwood Inference

From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: alice_wong <alice@borealishealth.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-18T17:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Align on private offer packaging and partner crediting

Hi all —

Two finance / compliance notes from our side:

1) PO and reseller margin: For audit purposes we need a signed PO that calls out the reseller margin amount or an attached reseller agreement. If procurement will accept the reseller margin as a credit line on the PO, that's sufficient.
2) Tax/invoicing: If the reseller is receiving a pass-through credit, we need to know the reseller's tax ID and invoice remit address to correctly annotate the settlement.
3) SLA exception: Because you referenced spikes, Borealis may request an SLA exception for higher burst capacity. I attached the "SLA-exception-request-form.pdf" — if you can complete and return with the PO we can evaluate for accelerated backfill and commit credits.

If procurement can circulate a PO by next Tuesday (2027-11-23) including the reseller margin line, we can prepare the DocuSign private offer and lock the commit band.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA-exception-request-form.pdf

From: Alice Wong <alice@borealishealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@borealishealth.com, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-19T10:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Align on private offer packaging and partner crediting

Sergio / Ben / Naomi —

Thanks — that all looks good. Procurement is comfortable with the single-token SKU and prefers the buffer credit approach. Action items from Borealis:

- Procurement will send a signed PO next Tuesday (2027-11-23) that includes a line noting an 11% reseller credit.
- We will provide reseller tax ID and remit information in the PO attachment.
- We will complete the SLA-exception form if Redwood indicates that will improve burst handling.

Please proceed with the DocuSign private offer draft and include the reseller credit line in the DocuSign metadata. Procurement, please review and confirm if you need the one-page summary Sergio mentioned — if so we'll need it before routing the PO.

Onward —
Alice Wong
Head of Cloud Procurement
Borealis Health
